Resolve, to Rename the Twin Rivers Fire Academy in Fairfield the Duane Bickford Fire Academy
Dear Senator Penny Beebe-Center, Representative Tavis Hasenfus and members of the Criminal Justice and Public Safety:
I, Robert Sezak, come before you as a former member of the Fairfield Town
Council, and as Somerset County Commissioner representing Fairfield and
Norridgewock to speak in favor renaming the Twin Rivers Fire Academy in Fairfield the Duane Bickford Fire Academy.
Chief Bickford was the major force in bringing the idea of an area fire training center to fruition. The planning for the facility started in 2013 and
the celebration of opening on July 19, 2022. His hard work and dedication in establishing this facility is important to fire departments and firefighters
throughout the state.
I believe that the facility named in his honor is well befitting the commitment and loyalty that Chief Duane Bickford has provided to the Town of Fairfield
and to firefighters everywhere.
Thank you for supporting this resolution.
Respectfully submitted,
Robert Sezak Somerset County Commissioner

Testimony of Senator Scott Cyrway
"LD 28 Resolve, to Rename the Twin Rivers Fire Academy in Fairfield the Duane Bickford Fire Academy"
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and my fellow members of the
Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee.
My name is Senator Scott Cyrway, and I represent district 16; Albion, Fairfield,
Oakland, Waterville, and Winslow.
I am proud to present this bill, Resolve, to Rename the Twin Rivers Fire Academy in
Fairfield the Duane Bickford Fire Academy.
Duane Bickford began his Firefighting career as a Volunteer Fire Fighter in 1987. In 2000, he was promoted to Fire Chief. After 23 years as Chief, Bickford retired in 2023. in November of 2024, he died at the age of 66.
Duane Bickford will always be remembered for the dedication he gave to his
community as a firefighter. I will always remember what he told me "|'ve never been one for speaking, but my heart has always been in this." Anyone who has interacted with him
knows this to be true.
An example of this is in Chief Bickford's pursuit of better training and training infrastructure in the state of Maine. This labor of love produced the Training Center in Fairfield we are discussing today. The planning center began in 2013, and in 2023 a Ribbon cutting ceremony marked the opening of the 500,000 dollar project. This training center does not simply serve the town of Fairfield, but it serves all Central Maine, filling a need for training centers in the region. This building, a great capstone to Chief Bickford's life work saves departments from driving to Bangor or southern Maine fortraining and provides a
place for all to improve their skills.
In addition to building the training center, Chief Bickford took time to train both new and old recruits personally at Kennebec Valley Community College. He also taught several
youth Firefighter recruitment classes.

He was a true leader and cared for his department's men and reputation. in my
interactions with Chief Bickford, he was always pleasant to talk to and shared pride for his
department and its personnel.
Chief Bickford dedicated his life to fire fighting in Maine. The Training Center in
Fairfield, he helped build, should bear his name so that we rememberthe work he did for our State. I ask you to accept a request for amendment by Shawn Esler, State Fire Marshall, to make the name The Duane Bickford Fire Training Facility. With that amendment, I ask you
to vote Ought to Pass.
Thank you for your time.

January 28, 2025
LD 28- Rename the Twin Rivers Fire Academy in Fairfield the Duane Bickford Fire
Academy
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and distinguished members of the Criminal
Justice and Public Safety Committee, I write in support of LD 28, with a slight amendment.
It is my recommendation to name the training facility the "Duane Bickford Fire Training Facility" .
I have consulted with Fire Chief Travis Leary of the Fairfield-Benton Fire Department, who confirmed
that the facility does not have a name. It is his request that the building itself be dedicated to the late Chief
Duane Bickford. In Chief Leary's words, "This will ensure that everyone that attends any form of training at this facility for as long as it remains, will see Chief Bickford's name attached."
Chief Leary further clarified that the "Twin Rivers Fire Academy" was an annual certification program
(Firefighter I & II) that Chief Bickford himself created in coordination with area Fire Chiefs. Chief Leary
would like to see that program, to include its name, continue. For clarity, the Twin Rivers Fire Academy (program) will be held at the Duane Bickford Fire Training Facility (training site and
building).
I write today, as both a representative of the Fire Service and as character reference, for Chief Bickford. Prior to his passing, I worked alongside him for over 20 years. Chief Bickford was educated, talented, dedicated, and always looked out for the best interest of his Fire Department and community.
From the idea of a regional training facility to its construction, Chief Bickford was instrumental in securing funding, communicating his ideas, soliciting involvement from area departments, and pushing forward to ensure a bright future training central Maine firefighters. With training being the highest
priority to increase safety and reduce liability, it is no doubt that Chief Bickford's efforts will impact the fire service for years to come. I will always remember his contribution to Maine's fire service and his
l
positive impact on my career.
I urge you to support and amend LD 28 to name the Duane Bickford Fire Training Facility in honor of
the late Chief Duane Bickford of Fairfield.
Please feel free to contact me with any questions at 441-9958.
